newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF talks stand-by loan with Ukraine, EFF later.
newsitem.headline: IMF talks stand-by loan with Ukraine, EFF later.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund announced on Thursday it was negotiating with Ukraine on an interim stand-by deal until Ukraine was ready for a long-term Extended Fund Facility, possibly by the end of the year.

"We are not there yet because some of the important measures are still absent, so therefore we are thinking of a bridging operation before going to the EFF," Adalbert Knobl, IMF mission chief to Ukraine, told Reuters.
He did not give any value for the stand-by loan.

Knobl said Ukraine had to fulfil several key conditions to qualify for the $2.5 to $3 billion EFF, such as approving personal income tax, lowering payroll taxes to 40 percent from 53 percent, charging 100 percent for communal services, and removal of privileges such as free bus rides for sectors of society.

Knobl said a mission would return on July 21 to discuss the stand-by loan with Ukraine after consulting management in Washington, and the loan could be approved by the end of August. The EFF could be issued by the end of the year or early 1998.

"I think that by suggesting there could be this bridging operation instead of the arrangement, it indicates the fund is trusting the Ukrainian authorities that in the period being bridged the macro-economic policies are put in place," he said.

The Fund said in a news release that "good progress" had been made at talks but added -- "In the meantime, we will continue to work with the government to be able to move to an EFF as soon as possible."
